name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-10.1
description: 10.1" 800x1280 MIPI-DSI panel (JD9365) with GT911 touch on an ESP32-P4, and Wi-Fi through its ESP32-C6. Compiled, not yet seen on a board.
verify: Nobody at LCD Wizard has had this board: the export for it compiles and has not been seen on the panel. Pins and the panel's start-up table are from Waveshare's own BSP (esp32_p4_wifi6_touch_lcd_x) and so are the settings (80 MHz, a VSYNC back porch of 10, 1500 Mbps a lane: what Waveshare's ESP-IDF code runs). If the screen stays dark with the backlight lit, try 60 MHz with a VSYNC back porch of 12 and 750 Mbps a lane, which is what GFX Library for Arduino's own definition of the board runs. These boards ship with ESP32-P4 chips of both generations. A design on this preset starts on revision 3, which Waveshare's own Arduino examples for the board build for; for a chip before revision 3 (the upload says "revision v1.x"), choose that under Hardware > Board > Chip revision. The touch controller may answer at 0x14 instead of 0x5D. Wi-Fi is the ESP32-C6 beside the P4, in the kit as the Wi-Fi co-processor on the ESP32 core's own SDIO lines (CLK 18, CMD 19, D0-D3 14-17, reset 54) - Waveshare publish no pins for it, and their own Arduino Wi-Fi example uses those defaults; it has to run ESP-Hosted of the core's release, which the board prints at start (see the README). Wi-Fi through it compiles and has not been on a board. Not driven: the TF card, the audio codec, the camera connector, and the C6's Bluetooth; ESP-NOW does not go through the C6.
